why: The `operation` string is only used as a lookup key into the in-memory operation registry (getOperation/isOperationAllowed in src/operations/registry.ts and access.ts) to return that operation's schema/example metadata; it never reaches a filesystem, network, shell, or eval sink.

Every enabled read operation (search_pages, get_page, get_page_markdown, query_database, get_block_children, list_file_uploads, get_file_upload, get_file_url, get_image, etc., across src/operations/*.ts) resolves caller ids/filters into JSON bodies sent to api.notion.com via the official @notionhq/client SDK (src/services/notion.ts); the two places that touch a URL directly, get_file_url and get_image in src/operations/files.ts, only ever resolve and fetch a Notion-minted signed URL for an object Notion hosts (URL_LIKE guard rejects a caller-supplied URL outright, and hosted/https checks gate the actual fetch), so there is no injection, path, or SSRF surface a caller controls.

sink: node:fs/promises readFile() on a caller-supplied absolute or ~-relative filesystem path, with the resulting bytes uploaded to Notion's file_uploads API and optionally attached to a page/block the caller names
guard: partial: resolveUploadPath() (src/operations/files.ts lines 95-111) only confines the path to NOTION_UPLOAD_ROOT when that env var is set; when it is unset -- the documented default ("Unset means no confinement, which is the behavior before this existed") -- expandHome() is applied and the raw path is read with no restriction at all
why: The `source.path` field is genuinely caller-controlled per upload_file's own zod schema and description ("Local filesystem path (absolute, or ~-relative)"), and every hop -- schema parse in dispatch/index.ts -> upload_file handler -> resolveUploadPath -> readFile -- was read. With NOTION_UPLOAD_ROOT unset (the out-of-the-box state), any caller able to invoke notion_write can read an arbitrary file the server process can read (SSH keys, .env, /etc/passwd, source) and exfiltrate its bytes by uploading it to Notion and attaching it to a page the caller can view -- a genuine confidentiality violation that exceeds the tool's advertised Notion-access contract, not mere robustness or a crash.
contract: Local path: `source: { type: "path", path: "/abs/or/~/file.pdf" }` (server reads the file directly -- preferred for local files; filename is derived from the path if omitted).
